## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9
    with:
      runtime_ref: a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9
    with:
      runtime_ref: a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
---

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | --- # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable AAA-styled first-person shooter in Three.js (“BLACKSITE // NIGHTFALL”) from scratch, since the repo contained no game code; iterate visually and finish the game.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at the end.
- Save screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest.
- Target “Call of Duty-level” quality per original issue prompt, including visual polish and a critical self-review loop.

## Decisions
- Built an original wave-based FPS: 5 assault waves, boss “WARDEN”, procedural map/props/textures, enemies, weapons, HUD, audio, menus, mobile touch support.
- Vendored Three.js r180 locally (`three.module.js` + newly added `three.core.js` and postprocessing addons) to avoid CDN dependency.
- Static `index.html` project (no package.json) so the runtime’s default static server works.
- Custom mission shell: menu/briefing/controls, pointer-lock FPS, pause/settings, death/victory stats, localStorage best score.
- Rendering: ACES tone mapping, bloom, custom grade shader (chromatic aberration, vignette, grain), fog, rain, lightning, floodlights, wet-ground reflections.
- Procedural WebAudio synthesis; no external audio assets.
- Optimizations added: instanced buttresses/razor wire/sandbags, reduced dynamic lights, enemy muzzle flashes without point lights.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `css/style.css`, all JS modules (`world.js`, `player.js`, `input.js`, `weapons.js`, `enemies.js`, `fx.js`, `hud.js`, `audio.js`, `main.js`) implemented.
- Local Three.js vendor files downloaded, including missing `vendor/three/three.core.js` that initially caused 404/module failure.
- Server running via tmux on port 3002; menu and gameplay render; no page errors after fixing `HUD.setAim`.
- Menu screenshot looks polished: title, typography, rain, moon, new courtyard-facing menu camera.
- Fixed loading delay to show menu ~2.9s after navigation (was ~5.1s, risking capture auto-start timeout).
- Fixed major gameplay bugs: missing `setAim`, reload duration, enemy head-hit offsets for heavy, material hit-flash reset, boss/audio issues.

### Active
- Visual/performance iteration from latest screenshots: scene still too dark, weapon view model too dark/unclear, floodlight cones removed but lighting needs tuning.
- Gameplay FPS measured ~7 under SwiftShader at 1280×800; needs further optimization or lower render cost.
- Verify wave flow after slow software rendering; wave 1 eventually starts but intermission progresses slowly under low FPS.
- Need fresh gameplay/combat/ADS screenshots after lighting changes and inspect.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/shots/game3.jpg` (latest gameplay/ADS screenshots may be `/tmp/opencode/shots/combat.jpg`, `ads2.jpg`) and assess brightness, weapon pose/readability, enemy visibility, HUD.
2. Improve scene lighting/exposure and weapon view-model lighting/pose; reduce heavy light/shadow cost (`shadowMap` size, spot/point count, bloom cost, pixel ratio).
3. Fix enemy visibility (lighter materials/rim light/emissive accents) and ensure crosshair contrast.
4. Verify full wave progression, win/lose overlays, pause/resume, weapon switch/reload/grenade, touch controls.
5. Run final capture-compatible smoke test; commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: markup, HUD/menu overlays, importmap, favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: all UI/HUD/menu styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: game loop, mission flow, postprocessing, menus, debug API `window.__nightfall`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: procedural level, textures, lighting, colliders, rain.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/weapons.js`: view models, firing/ADS/reload/grenades.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/enemies.js`: soldier models, AI, waves, boss, raycast.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/player.js`: movement/collision/health/camera.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/hud.js`: HUD, radar, killfeed, stats.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/fx.js`: tracers, impacts, particles, explosions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/pointer lock/touch.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three/`: vendored Three.js + addons.
- `/tmp/opencode/shot3.mjs`: latest Playwright screenshot harness.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/`: latest screenshots (`menu3.jpg`, `game3.jpg`, `combat.jpg`, `ads2.jpg`).

## Important Context
- Server: `tmux new-session -d -s nightfall "cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround && PORT=3002 node \$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs 2>&1 | tee /tmp/opencode/server.log"`; logs at `/tmp/opencode/server.log`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable AAA-styled first-person shooter in Three.js (“BLACKSITE // NIGHTFALL”) from scratch, iterate visually, and finish the game.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at the end.
- Save screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest.
- Target “Call of Duty-level” quality per original issue prompt, including visual polish and a critical self-review loop.

## Decisions
- Built an original wave-based FPS: 5 assault waves, boss “WARDEN”, procedural map/props/textures, enemies, weapons, HUD, audio, menus, mobile touch support.
- Vendored Three.js r180 locally (`three.module.js`, `three.core.js`, postprocessing addons) to avoid CDN dependency.
- Static `index.html` project (no package.json) so the runtime’s default static server works.
- Custom mission shell: menu/briefing/controls, pointer-lock FPS, pause/settings, death/victory stats, localStorage best score.
- Rendering: ACES tone mapping, bloom, custom grade shader (chromatic aberration, vignette, grain), fog, rain, lightning, floodlights, wet-ground reflections.
- Procedural WebAudio synthesis; no external audio assets.
- Optimizations: instanced buttresses/razor wire/sandbags, reduced dynamic lights, 1024 moon shadow map, dimmer bloom, enemy muzzle flashes without point lights.
- Weapon view model now scaled 0.64, repositioned for readability; ADS pulls weapon forward (rifle ads z -0.56, pistol -0.54); added holo reticle canvas, boss aura, moon texture, darker gun materials.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `css/style.css`, all JS modules (`world.js`, `player.js`, `input.js`, `weapons.js`, `enemies.js`, `fx.js`, `hud.js`, `audio.js`, `main.js`) implemented.
- Fixed missing `HUD.setAim`, enemy head offsets, reload duration, boss/audio issues.
- Fixed major visual issue: giant orange bloom from flashlight/lens; reduced flashlight intensity/angle, bloom strength/threshold, and re-lit the weapon.
- Added procedural moon texture with craters, WARDEN red aura light, darker/lower-metalness gun materials, subtle holo glass, new reticle sprite; floodlight glow sprites shrunk.
- Fixed critical wave progression bug: `enemies.onAllDead` was never wired; added `this.enemies.onAllDead = (n) => this.onWaveCleared(n)` in `main.js`.
- Fixed death/pause bug: pointer-lock loss during fatal damage could pause instead of entering dying state; `onLockChange` now ignores pause if `this.player.dead`.
- Verified full flow: waves 1–5 spawn/clear, WARDEN boss spawns with boss bar/banner, victory transitions to `won` and shows “MISSION ACCOMPLISHED” stats.
- Verified reload (mag refills, reserve decreases), weapon switch, grenade throw, pause/resume, death → “MISSION FAILED” overlay, and zero page errors.
- NPC/weapon visuals improved and screenshots captured: `/tmp/opencode/shots/x-play.jpg`, `x-ads.jpg`, `x-lose.jpg`, `z-boss.jpg`, `z-win.jpg`, `v-pause.jpg`, `x-mobileplay.jpg`.
- Performance measured ~30–39 fps under SwiftShader during normal gameplay (menu ~73).

### Active
- Mobile portrait HUD layout still cramped: rotate hint overlaps top HUD, radar/objective/vitals overlap joystick, weapon info collides with touch buttons.
- Need a final visual review after latest light/material adjustments and final capture-compatible smoke test.
- Need to commit all changes (still uncommitted on `opencode/42106635640`).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `/tmp/opencode/mobilebounds.mjs` to measure mobile element boxes, then add portrait CSS fixes: hide `.rotate-hint`, shrink/reposition top HUD, move vitals above the joystick, and keep ammo clear of touch buttons.
2. Inspect latest desktop `x-play.jpg`/`x-ads.jpg` and optionally retune weapon tan/lighting and the bright hazard-stripe blastwall.
3. Re-run final flow/smoke test (wave progression, victory, death, reload, pause, no page errors) and capture final screenshots.
4. Commit the completed game files.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: markup, HUD/menu overlays, importmap, favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: all UI/HUD/mobile styling; portrait issues here.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: game loop, wave flow, victory/death, postprocessing, debug API; contains `onAllDead` and death-pause fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/weapons.js`: view models, flashlight, holo reticle, ADS poses, firing/reload/grenades.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: procedural level, moon texture, env map, lighting, colliders, rain.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/enemies.js`: soldier models, AI, waves, WARDEN boss aura, raycast.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/player.js`: movement/collision/health/camera.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/hud.js`: HUD, radar, killfeed, banners, result stats.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/fx.js`: pooled tracers, impacts, particles, explosions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/pointer lock/touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three/`: vendored Three.js + addons.
- `/tmp/opencode/quick.mjs`: fast deploy + gameplay screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/finish.mjs`: wave progression, boss, victory, death flow tests.
- `/tmp/opencode/verify.mjs`: reload/fire/death/mobile verification.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobilebounds.mjs`: new mobile HUD bounding-box probe, not yet run.

## Important Context
- Server: `tmux new-session -d -s nightfall "cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround && PORT=3002 node \$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs 2>&1 | tee /tmp/opencode/server.log"`; logs at `/tmp/opencode/server.log`.
- Playwright: use `DISPLAY=:0`, Chromium config from `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`.
- Capture auto-start only recognizes button labels exactly matching start/play (or aria-label); Deploy button has `aria-label="Play Now"`.
- `window.__nightfall` exposes `start`, `state_info`, `spawn`, `killAll`, `god`, `heal`, `teleport`, `fire`, `damagePlayer`, plus `game/player/enemies/weapons/world/hud`.
- Under SwiftShader, gameplay runs ~5–35 fps; at 5 fps the `dt` cap makes intermissions/reloads take much longer in real time, so tests should force `g.intermission=0.1` or quick-forward `weapons.update(0.05)`.
- To test ADS via DOM, set `game.input.mouse.right = true` (input.aim is a getter, assigning does nothing).
- Reload test confirmed: mag 4 → 30, reserve 180 → 154, `reloading=false`, after 60 × `weapons.update(0.05)`.
- Death test after fix: state `dying` → `gameover`, overlay visible, title “MISSION FAILED”, kicker “OPERATOR KIA”.
- Touch test: `isTouch:true`, touch controls visible, state `playing`.
- Changes are uncommitted; branch `opencode/42106635640`.
